The retrieved evidence does not support a blanket claim that video games are harmful to children's mental health; instead, the findings are mixed. Moderate gaming was reported to fare best on mental health outcomes in one study, while excessive gaming showed mild increases in problematic behaviors, and another source says some games can improve mood, relaxation, anxiety, and resilience [d2][d8].

At the same time, some snippets report possible harms, especially with excessive or violent gaming, including aggression-related concerns or problems for vulnerable children [d1][d5]. Other evidence says harms may be concentrated in a small minority of children with pre-existing personality or mental health problems rather than the vast majority [d1][d3].

So, based on these snippets, video games are not uniformly harmful; effects appear to depend on factors like amount of play, game content, and the child’s vulnerabilities [d1][d2][d8].
